text.p: Nigeria national coach Amodu Shaibu has been suspended indefinitely by his country's soccer authorities, state television reported on Sunday.
No reason was given for the ban which takes immediate effect and was ordered by Sports minister Jim Nwobodo. A replacement for Shaibu has not yet been named.

Nigerian Football Association (NFA) technical committee member Emeka Inyama said: "The sports minister may have ordered the suspension following a letter of query given to Shaibu after he criticised the sports authorities last week."
Shaibu said in a television interview last week that "the NFA and sports ministry officials are not telling the truth about soccer matters in Nigeria."

The relationship between Shaibu and the sports authorities has not been smooth since October when he was asked to take temporary charge of the team while a permanent replacement was sought for Dutchman Jo Bonfrere.
Bonfrere quit the job in October alleging poor treatment and interference in his duties by the sports authorities.
